designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Strong, clean system: consistent monoline icons on a tight 4x4 grid, condensed caps labels, and a full-width heavy headline that anchors the block and reads from 3 m. But the punchline is jammed against the last label row (barely 20px of air at full size, much less than the inter-row gaps), so the grid and the verdict blur into one mass instead of 'evidence, then conclusion'. The airbag icon's solid disc is heavier than every other glyph and pulls the eye, and in one ink nothing reads as 'lit', so it looks a little like a reference chart.
designs.fix: Open a clear gap above PROBABLY FINE. (at least one icon-row gap, roughly 1.5-2x the current row spacing) so the headline stands apart as the payoff; while there, redraw the airbag disc as an outline to match the stroke weight.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: The best typography of the three: a tracked serif all-caps title, a small crescent as the hinge, and warm italic serif captions that give the deadpan instruction-manual voice. The brush line is lively but consistent in weight, the repetition of 'Turn around.' carries the gag, and the single centred step 7 closes the zig-zag reading path neatly. Weaknesses are minor: the title is wider than the drawings column so the block is slightly top-heavy, and the vertical rhythm drifts (gaps between rows 1-2, 3-4 and 5-6 are not equal; drawings sit on uneven baselines).
designs.fix: Normalise the grid: give each pair of drawings a shared baseline and equal row spacing so captions line up on a steady rhythm, and narrow the title tracking a touch so its width matches the illustration column.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Clear three-beat comic structure with a good scale shift: two small set-up panels, then a large payoff panel where the box and bed break the frame. Line work is confident and the cat's smug face lands. But the caption, the actual joke, is tiny and light relative to the heavy art and becomes unreadable from 3 m on the tee. The frame break is also muddled: the box's left face lines up with the panel's left border and the frame line runs on behind the bed, so it reads as a drawing error rather than a deliberate breakout.
designs.fix: Set BOX NOT SOLD SEPARATELY. much bigger and heavier (roughly the width of the two top panels, bold condensed) so it weighs as much as panel 3; secondarily, push the box clearly past the frame on the left so the breakout reads as intentional.
